newsitem.title: USA: Ohio wheat development rebounds from previous week.
newsitem.headline: Ohio wheat development rebounds from previous week.

text.p: Winter wheat development in Ohio improved substantially from the previous week, as of Sunday, according to the Ohio Agricultural Statistics Service.

Sixty percent of the crop was turning color, up 51 percentage points from the previous week and up one point from a year ago. The five-year average was 79 percent. Winter wheat was starting to ripen, but was about 11 days behind average.
Winter wheat was rated 65 percent good to excellent, compared with 63 percent last week.
Corn condition was rated 63 percent good to excellent, up from 59 percent a week earlier.

Soybean planting was 99 percent complete, up from 95 percent a week earlier and slightly ahead of the 98 percent average. Soybeans were blooming on one percent of the acreage versus zero last year and five percent average. Emergence was at 95 percent, well ahead of last year's 70 percent and slightly ahead of the average of 91 percent.
Soybeans were rated 56 percent good or excellent, up from 53 percent a week earlier.

Topsoil moisture as of Friday, June 27, was rated one percent very short, 11 percent short, 78 percent adequate and 10 percent surplus, a 22-point decrease in surplus from the previous week, the report said.

There were 5.7 days suitable for fieldwork during the week ended on Friday. This was the highest value since the first week of April and is greater than the five-year average of 5.3 days, the report said. There were 3.9 days suitable for fieldwork in the previous week.
